comm.t: The gods’ hymn on the Himālaya (5.9–82) is over, and Medhas, still speaking to King Suratha, returns to the story: what happened while the gods were praising.

samasa.sense: occupied with hymns and other acts of worship

samasa.literal: a king’s delight, i.e. a king’s son
samasa.sense: O prince — Medhas’s address to Suratha

morph.note: Perfect of √या (ययौ, with the -au ending of ā-roots) behind two prefixes: अभि + आ, where i becomes y before ā (अभ्या-). ‘Came up to, approached’.
Infinitive in -tum of √स्ना, expressing purpose with a verb of motion: ‘came to bathe’.
With the participle-like adjective स्तवादियुक्तानाम् it forms a genitive absolute: ‘the gods being so engaged’, i.e. ‘while the gods were praising’.

mantras.anvaya: नृपनन्दन, एवं देवानां स्तवादियुक्तानां (सताम्) तत्र पार्वती जाह्नव्याः तोये स्नातुम् अभ्याययौ।
mantras.anvaya_en: A genitive absolute (एवं … देवानाम्) sets the time; the main clause is पार्वती … अभ्याययौ with the purpose infinitive स्नातुम्; नृपनन्दन is the narrator’s address.
mantras.lit: While the gods were thus engaged in praise and the rest, there Pārvatī came, O son of a king, to bathe in the water of the Jāhnavī.
mantras.tr: While the gods were thus praising, O prince, Pārvatī came there to bathe in the waters of the Gaṅgā.

comm.t: The scene shifts while the hymn is still in the air: Pārvatī, Śiva’s consort and the daughter of Himavat, comes down to the Gaṅgā to bathe at the very place where the gods are praying. The genitive absolute ties the two events together.

Chapter 4 announced this episode in advance: the Goddess would arise again ‘from the body of Gaurī’ to kill Śumbha and Niśumbha (4.41, गौरीदेहात्). Pārvatī’s coming to the river is the occasion for that promise to be kept.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has the same name, पार्वती (name 246). The two works share the Śākta identification of the Goddess with Himavat’s daughter; they remain distinct texts.

sandhi.note: After a vowel other than a/ā the visarga (as रु) is sounded r before a voiced consonant.
-e + a- → -e’-: the initial a is elided (avagraha).
Visarga before c becomes s, and s next to c becomes ś (-तश्च); then च + अस्याः → चास्याः.
ā + a → ā; then final t before ś becomes c, and the ś after it becomes ch: अब्रवीत् शिवा → अब्रवीच्छिवा.

samasa.sense: the bodily envelope, out of which the new form steps
samasa.alt: Also read as a karmadhāraya of identification, शरीरम् एव कोशः ‘the body, which is a sheath’; the sense is the same.

morph.note: Imperfect of √ब्रू with augment a- and the connecting ī that ब्रू takes before consonant endings of the strong forms: अ-ब्रव्-ई-त्. The verse uses it twice, once for each speaker.
Passive present of √स्तु: the root vowel is lengthened before the passive suffix -ya- (स्तू-य-ते). With the instrumental भवद्भिः: ‘who is praised by you?’.
The suffix -tas (tasil) makes an indeclinable with ablative sense: ‘from the body’s sheath’. It still governs a genitive (अस्याः), as a noun would.

mantras.anvaya: सुभ्रूः सा तान् सुरान् अब्रवीत् — अत्र भवद्भिः का स्तूयते (इति)। अस्याः शरीरकोशतः समुद्भूता शिवा च अब्रवीत्।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two sentences of the same shape: subject, अब्रवीत्. The first carries Pārvatī’s question as direct speech; the second introduces the answer, which is given in 5.86.
mantras.lit: She, the fair-browed one, said to those gods: ‘Who is being praised by you here?’ And Śivā, having come forth from the sheath of her body, said:
mantras.tr: The lovely-browed Goddess asked the gods, ‘Whom are you praising here?’ And from the sheath of her own body Śivā came forth and answered:

comm.t: Pārvatī asks whom the gods are praising, and the answer comes not from them but from a goddess who steps out of Pārvatī’s own body. The one who asks and the one who answers are of one substance; the reply follows in 5.86.
Traditionally the question is read as the Goddess’s play (līlā): she asks as though she did not know, so that she herself may reveal that the gods’ hymn was addressed to her.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) also names the Goddess सुभ्रूः (name 461) and शिवा (name 53). The shared epithets belong to a common Śākta vocabulary; the two texts are separate.

morph.note: Passive present of √कृ: before the passive -ya- the root’s ṛ becomes ri (क्रि-य-ते). ‘Is being made’.
सम् + आ + √इ + kta: आ + इत → एत by guṇa (6.1.87), so समेत ‘come together, assembled’.
Past participle of परा + √जि, ‘conquered, defeated’, construed with the agent instrumental निशुम्भेन.

mantras.anvaya: शुम्भदैत्यनिराकृतैः समरे निशुम्भेन पराजितैः समेतैः देवैः एतत् मम स्तोत्रं क्रियते।
mantras.anvaya_en: A passive sentence: subject स्तोत्रम्, verb क्रियते, agent देवैः with three qualifiers (निराकृतैः, समेतैः, पराजितैः).
mantras.lit: This hymn to me is being made by the gods, assembled, driven out by the daitya Śumbha and defeated in battle by Niśumbha.
mantras.tr: ‘This hymn is offered to me by the gods, who have gathered here after the demon Śumbha drove them out and Niśumbha defeated them in battle.’
mantras.tr_note: ‘After’ makes explicit the order of events implied by the three participles.

comm.t: Śivā answers Pārvatī’s question: the hymn is hers. The gods are named by their plight — expelled by Śumbha, beaten in battle by Niśumbha — which recalls the opening of the chapter (5.2–5).

The tradition reads the episode as a statement of identity: the Goddess the gods invoked as dwelling in all beings (5.14–80) answers from within Pārvatī herself. Asking and answering, she shows that the hymn and its object are hers.

samasa.literal: from the sheath of the body
samasa.sense: as in 5.85, here in the ablative case form

morph.note: Taddhita: कोश + the affix -ika with vṛddhi of the first vowel (को → कौ), feminine in -ī: ‘she who belongs to (came from) the sheath’. The verse itself gives the etymology.
Passive present of √गै: the root appears as गी before the passive -ya- (गी-य-ते), ‘is sung, is celebrated’.
निस् + √सृ + kta, feminine: ‘issued forth’. The participle carries the action without an auxiliary verb.

mantras.anvaya: यत् तस्याः पार्वत्याः शरीरकोशात् अम्बिका निःसृता, ततः (सा) समस्तेषु लोकेषु कौशिकी इति गीयते।
mantras.anvaya_en: A causal pair: यत् … निःसृता (‘since she came forth …’) and ततः … गीयते (‘therefore she is sung of …’).
mantras.lit: Since Ambikā came forth from the sheath of the body of that Pārvatī, she is therefore sung of in all the worlds as ‘Kauśikī’.
mantras.tr: Because Ambikā emerged from the sheath of Pārvatī’s body, she is celebrated in all the worlds as Kauśikī.

comm.t: Medhas explains the name: the goddess who emerged (Śivā of 5.85, now called Ambikā) is Kauśikī because she came out of Pārvatī’s bodily sheath (kośa). From here the text mostly calls her Ambikā or Devī.

In the Gita Press pāṭha, the dhyāna printed before chapter 5 describes the presiding Goddess of the third carita, Mahāsarasvatī, as गौरीदेहसमुद्भवाम् ‘born from the body of Gaurī’ — this very emergence. The assignment of Mahāsarasvatī to the carita is liturgical tradition.

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) also calls the Goddess अम्बिका (name 295). The Devī Māhātmya’s own story of Kauśikī belongs to this text; the shared name does not import the other hymn’s theology.
